body: Tool-call lines come from the transcript read by the session agent (option a), no PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks. Measured: records become visible 0.1-0.3 s after their timestamp (claude -p median ~0.13 s; live interactive subagent transcript median 0.16 s, max 0.28 s); in an interactive main transcript the assistant record (text + tool_use) is only written when the tool finishes (4.6-6.6 s lag on a 3 s tool, the user's 4-7 s), but the tool_result right after it is visible 0.10-0.19 s after the tool ends, so a finished-call line is as timely as a PostToolUse hook. Hook cost per tool call: ~17-19 ms with a live hub, ~530 ms with the hub down (dev build, Windows). Alternative: PostToolUse hook for the instant line plus transcript for history (a process per tool call, 0.5 s stall per call when the hub is down, same moment).

The hub owns the stream offset (registry sessions[..].stream.offset = transcript bytes whose messages Telegram has answered, plus pending tool calls and 👀 receipts); the agent is stateless and answers each hub transcript_read {session_id, path, from} with one transcript_chunk of complete lines as transcript::stream_events. A hub restart re-reads from the answered offset (at most the messages in flight repeat), an agent restart (resume) is served from the same offset. Alternative: agent-owned offsets pushed continuously (needs an ack protocol and state across agent processes; a new agent after /resume would not know it).

✍ evidence is the session's own transcript: a meta user record (or a queued_command attachment) whose <channel ...> opening tag has message_id=N, for an N the hub handed to that session's agent (receipts, persisted, 32 max). UserPromptSubmit is not used for reactions at all. Alternative: a UserPromptSubmit hook that extracts message_id from the prompt (unverified that it fires for channel messages; a second parser of the channel tag in the hook).

Merging of tool-call lines lives in the scheduler: Op::Stream{merge:true} lines of one topic queued behind the head line join its message only when more messages wait than the bucket has tokens, never across another message of that topic, within 4096 UTF-16 units; merged jobs answer Outcome::Merged. Permission prompts overtake stream lines of their own topic (not ordinary messages). Alternative: batching in the slots actor (it cannot see the bucket or the queue).

A Stop answer of a streamed session is held until the chunk of the first transcript read issued after the Stop is handed out (max Options.hold_answer 1.5 s), so the turn's last tool lines come before the answer. Alternative: send at once (the last line can land after the answer when the answer follows the last tool result within one poll interval, 300 ms).

Terminal-typed prompts and slash commands stream as '> text' (brief form); Telegram-originated prompts are not echoed (only reactions). Assistant text streams only with stop_reason tool_use; end_turn/null text is left to the Stop hook. Alternative: tool lines only (the Telegram reader sees answers to prompts it never saw).

Call order: open tool calls are kept in call order (persisted Stream.calls); a result marks its call done and only the done calls at the head are sent, so Result(B) before Result(A) waits for A. A prompt, a note or a turn end flushes the turn (done calls in call order, calls without a result are not shown); a call past MAX_CALLS=64 lets the oldest go the same way. Alternative: PLAN_V2's 'stop read-ahead at the cap' (deadlocks: the flush marker is further in the file than the stopped read).

Offset commit: every read ends with a barrier (offset + snapshot of open calls); it is persisted only when every stream message before it was answered Sent/Merged. A refused message (network, 5xx, lost topic) stops commits; once nothing is in flight the stream rewinds to the last committed barrier after Options.stream_retry (5 s), so order holds and lines come at least once. A 4xx that is not a lost topic is skipped with one warning (a message Telegram never takes must not block the stream). The scheduler answers Merged only after the merged send succeeded, otherwise the merged receivers close. Alternative: retry the single failed job (later lines already queued would overtake it).

Stop barrier: transcript::stream_events emits TurnEnd for an assistant text record whose stop_reason is set and not tool_use (the thinking record of the same response has no text block, so one TurnEnd per final text). A Stop of a streamed session is held in a FIFO (max 8) until a TurnEnd is read, then goes after the lines before it; a TurnEnd read before its Stop is counted (ends_unclaimed, cleared by a new prompt or a matched channel record) and lets that Stop go at once; a blank Stop still takes its turn end; Options.hold_answer (5 s) bounds the wait. Alternatives: prompt_id correlation (assistant records carry no promptId; Stop.prompt_id unverified), PLAN.md's first-read-after-Stop with 1.5 s (lets late tool lines follow the answer).

Finding 4 (tool errors shown as ✓ when is_error is absent) not reproduced: 9,661 real tool_result blocks in the 400 newest local transcripts; every <tool_use_error> (10) and every string toolUseResult starting 'Error:' or 'User rejected' (313) has is_error: true; is_error is absent only on tool_reference results (ToolSearch) and MCP results, where treating 'Error' text or a string toolUseResult as failure would mark successful MCP calls ✗. Code left as is (is_error == true).

Path gate: the agent reads only a file whose canonical path is <canonical root>/<one dir>/<session_id>.jsonl with root = CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects, else USERPROFILE|HOME/.claude/projects, and that is a regular file; missing or foreign = missing. Replacement/truncation: a read from offset N answers reset when N > len or byte N-1 is not a newline; the hub warns once and reads from 0 (repeat possible, no loss). Alternative: file identity (windows-sys file id / dev+ino) plus a 4 KiB checkpoint (platform code for a case Claude Code never produces).

Request ids on transcript_read/chunk not added: a late chunk of a timed-out read carries `from`, and the hub accepts a chunk only when from == read_at and it comes on the connection the read went to (added), so a stale answer is either still a valid read of the same bytes or dropped.

Agent reads are serialized: one reader task per agent process with a request slot of 1; the channel loop try_sends and drops a request while one waits (the hub asks again after 10 s or on a new connection), so there is at most one blocking read and one queued. Stream messages count in queued_messages and the stream takes no new line while 128 (MAX_QUEUED_MESSAGES/2) wait or 64 of its own do (the rest stays in the file); reactions are capped at 64 in flight. Alternative: per-request spawn_blocking (unbounded blocking reads on timeouts).

Rated unbounded Live.waiting barrier growth (a barrier with a calls snapshot per idle 300 ms read while a stream message waits for Telegram) as the one blocking finding; proposed fix: coalesce consecutive barriers in Live::barrier (replace a trailing Barrier). Alternative: stop polling while any stream message of the session waits (delays tool lines and held answers behind the 20/min queue).

[Request interrupted by user...] (and the 'for tool use' variant) streams as a Note (plain text, flushes finished calls, no NewTurn), not as '> prompt'. Alternative: skip it entirely (the topic would get no sign that the turn stopped, and no Stop answer comes after an interrupt).

A missing transcript logs at debug only for the first episode of a stream that never saw the file and reads from byte 0 (Live.file_seen, kept across rewind); every other missing episode keeps the single warn. Evidence: in the 60 newest local transcripts the file birth time equals the first prompt's timestamp (within ~2 s), so a new session has no file until its first prompt. Alternative: key on the committed registry offset == 0 (a file seen but not yet committed would then stay quiet when deleted).

QA end-to-end drives the real cctg agent binary over real TCP into serve_agents (plus real Slots and Scheduler, fake Telegram) instead of feeding AgentEvent into Slots directly as every unit test and stream_logs do. Alternative: in-process AgentEvent injection, which cannot see ingress filtering. This exposed that ingress drops every transcript_chunk.

Verifying streaming end to end at HEAD is impossible: serve_agents forwards only Reply/PermissionRequest/PermissionAck, so each TranscriptChunk is logged as agent repeated its handshake; ignored and the hub re-asks every 10 s. The remaining criteria were checked with a local one-line ingress patch (TranscriptChunk added to the forwarded arm), reverted with git checkout afterwards.

M2 fixed in the scheduler, not by one stream message in flight per session: one-in-flight leaves nothing queued to merge and breaks the merge-at-the-limit criterion. A stream line that fails with anything but a Telegram 4xx breaks its topic stream in the scheduler: queued and later lines of that thread are dropped unsent until a line marked restart (first message of a Live, i.e. after a rewind) arrives. 4xx is excluded because the actor counts it as skipped/accepted; breaking on it would loop.

ends_unclaimed receipt loss: a new prompt or channel record no longer zeroes unclaimed turn ends; they stay claimable for hold_answer after the new turn is read, then lapse. Alternative kept: zeroing (loses the claim when Stop reaches the actor after the next prompt chunk, answer then waits for the next turn end or 5 s). Cost of the choice: a lost Stop lets the next turn answer go early if it comes within hold_answer.

QA2 refusal e2e with a small bucket (merged stream messages) did not kill the M2-revert mutation (break_stream no-op): the refused merged message already carried every queued line, so nothing could overtake it. A second e2e with a fast bucket and one refused unmerged line with the rest queued behind it kills the mutation.

The answer-overtakes-lines-after-a-refusal finding is kept as a failing QA2 e2e test (qa2_answer_after_a_refused_line_still_follows_its_lines) and rated minor (failure path only, nothing lost, lines stay in order among themselves, answer reappears context after stream_retry). Alternative: rate it blocking as a violation of the answer-after-lines promise; rejected because it needs a non-4xx Telegram refusal in the turn window and PLAN_FINAL already accepts answer/line reordering on rewind.
